chunks: 5102 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who came to another man and said, “So-and-so sent me to you so that you may send to him such-and-such,” so he gave it to him and believed him. Then he met his companion and said to him, “Indeed, your messenger came to me, so I sent with him to you such-and-such and such-and-such.” He said, “I did not send him to you, nor did anyone bring me anything.” Then the messenger claimed that he had indeed sent him and that he had delivered it to him. He said:

“If he finds proof against him that he never sent him, his hand is cut off. But if he does not find proof against him, then his oath is by Allah that he did not send him, and the other recovers the property from the messenger.”
I said, “Then if he claims that need drove him to that?” He said, “His hand is cut off, because he stole the man’s property.”

key_terms.الرَّسُولُ: the claimed messenger who received and carried the property
key_terms.الْحَاجَةُ: need or necessity, claimed here as a motive
key_terms.الْمَالَ: the property or wealth that was taken
key_terms.بَيِّنَةً: legal proof or evidentiary proof establishing the claim
key_terms.سَرَقَ: he stole, indicating the act is legally treated as theft
key_terms.فَيَمِينُهُ: his oath, used here as a formal legal denial

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone takes wealth by falsely claiming to be another person’s messenger?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person who fraudulently takes property by falsely claiming to be a messenger. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between cases with proof and without proof, and affirms the owner’s right to recover his wealth. It also makes clear that poverty or need does not negate the ruling when the act is treated as theft of another person’s property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5102 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who went to another man and said: "So-and-so sent me to you to collect such-and-such," and the man gave it to him, believing him.
Later, he met the original person and said: "Your messenger came to me, and I sent with him such-and-such," but the man replied:
"I did not send him to you, nor did anyone bring me anything."
The supposed messenger then claimed that he had indeed been sent and had delivered the item to him.

Imam (as) said: "If proof is established against him that he was never sent, his hand is to be cut off. But if there is no proof, the man must swear by Allah (swt) that he did not send him, and the other must recover his money from the messenger."

I asked: "What if he claims that necessity compelled him to do so?"
Imam (as) replied: "His hand is to be cut off because he has stolen the man's wealth."
